```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Two rxode2 messages are expected here and only these are muffled. The
# between-occasion etas enter ka and F as an indicator-weighted sum, so rxode2
# reports them as 'non-mu referenced' whenever the model is parsed (this only
# affects estimation speed-ups). Typical-value solves of several subjects with
# zeroRe() report a simulation 'without omega'.
muffle_expected <- function(w) {
  msg <- conditionMessage(w)
  if (grepl("non-mu referenced", msg, fixed = TRUE) ||
      grepl("without 'omega'", msg, fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
mod <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Usansky_2026_brensocatib")),
  warning = muffle_expected
)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r mod$reference`
* Description: `r mod$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70340> (open access; the NONMEM
  control stream of the final model is Data S1 of the supplement)

Brensocatib is an oral, reversible inhibitor of dipeptidyl peptidase 1 (DPP1)
developed for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis. Usansky 2026 pooled 11
clinical trials to support the 10 and 25 mg once-daily doses in adults and in
adolescents aged 12 years and older.

# Population

The analysis data set held 11,643 plasma concentrations from 1098
participants: 291 healthy volunteers, 783 patients with non-cystic fibrosis
bronchiectasis (31 of them adolescents aged 12 to < 18 years) and 24 patients
with cystic fibrosis (Usansky 2026 Table 1). It came from eight phase 1 trials
(single doses 5-120 mg, including food-effect, hepatic- and renal-impairment and
drug-interaction studies), two phase 2 trials (NCT05090904 and WILLOW) and the
phase 3 ASPEN trial (NCT04594369, 10 or 25 mg once daily). Mean age was 51
years and mean weight 69.2 kg; 55.4% were female, 71.8% White, 11.6% Asian and
6.0% Black.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Usansky_2026_brensocatib")()$population`.

# Reference-subject and extreme-scenario exposures

The forest-plot reference subject is a healthy 49-year-old White male of 70 kg,
fasted, without hepatic impairment or interacting comedication, taking 25 mg
once daily (Usansky 2026 Results). The paper gives his steady-state AUC24 as
3723 ng h/mL and Cmax as 246 ng/mL, and gives the two highest-exposure
scenarios, a 12-year-old 30 kg female taking verapamil or clarithromycin. These
are geometric means of 1000 simulated subjects; with log-normal random effects
the geometric mean of AUC equals the typical-value AUC, so the typical-value
model is the right comparator.

The steady-state helpers below dose once daily for 21 days (more than 10
half-lives) and observe the final 24-hour interval.

```{r helpers}
tau <- 24
n_days <- 21
t_ss <- (n_days - 1) * tau

make_ss_events <- function(subjects, dose, obs_step = 0.1) {
  obs_times <- seq(t_ss, t_ss + tau, by = obs_step)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(subjects, time = seq(0, t_ss, by = tau)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(subjects, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(DOSE = dose) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dplyr::everything()) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ss_nca <- function(sim, events, group) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dplyr::all_of(group))
  dose <- events |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dplyr::all_of(group))
  fml_c <- stats::as.formula(paste("Cc ~ time |", group, "+ id"))
  fml_d <- stats::as.formula(paste("amt ~ time |", group, "+ id"))
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = t_ss, end = t_ss + tau,
    auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
  )
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, fml_c),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, fml_d),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
}

reference_covariates <- tibble::tibble(
  WT = 70, AGE = 49, SEXF = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0, HEPIMP = 0,
  FED = 0, FORM_SOLUTION = 0, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 0,
  CONMED_CLARITHROMYCIN = 0, CONMED_VERAPAMIL = 0,
  STUDY_PHASE2 = 0, STUDY_PHASE3 = 0, OCC = 1
)
```

The scenario table follows the rows of Usansky 2026 Figures 3 and 4. "Adolescent"
is 12 years and "elderly" 85 years; the low and high body weights are 30 and
155 kg (the figure labels).

```{r scenarios}
scenario <- function(label, ...) {
  dplyr::mutate(reference_covariates, scenario = label, ...)
}
scenarios <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  scenario("Reference"),
  scenario("Fed", FED = 1),
  scenario("High body weight: 155 kg", WT = 155),
  scenario("Low body weight: 30 kg", WT = 30),
  scenario("Received rif", CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 1),
  scenario("Received clari", CONMED_CLARITHROMYCIN = 1),
  scenario("Received verap", CONMED_VERAPAMIL = 1),
  scenario("Female", SEXF = 1),
  scenario("Female: 155 kg", SEXF = 1, WT = 155),
  scenario("Female: 30 kg", SEXF = 1, WT = 30),
  scenario("Black", RACE_BLACK = 1),
  scenario("Asian", RACE_ASIAN = 1),
  scenario("Hepatic impairment", HEPIMP = 1),
  scenario("Elderly: 85 years old", AGE = 85),
  scenario("Adolescent: 12 years old", AGE = 12),
  scenario("Elderly female: 85 years old", AGE = 85, SEXF = 1),
  scenario("Adolescent female: 12 years old", AGE = 12, SEXF = 1),
  scenario("Black male: 155 kg, rif, hepatically impaired",
           RACE_BLACK = 1, WT = 155, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 1, HEPIMP = 1),
  scenario("Asian male: 155 kg, rif, hepatically impaired",
           RACE_ASIAN = 1, WT = 155, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 1, HEPIMP = 1),
  scenario("Black male: 85 y, 155 kg, nonfasting, rif, hepatically impaired",
           RACE_BLACK = 1, AGE = 85, WT = 155, FED = 1,
           CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 1, HEPIMP = 1),
  scenario("Asian male: 85 y, 155 kg, nonfasting, rif, hepatically impaired",
           RACE_ASIAN = 1, AGE = 85, WT = 155, FED = 1,
           CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 1, HEPIMP = 1),
  scenario("Female: 30 kg, clari", SEXF = 1, WT = 30, CONMED_CLARITHROMYCIN = 1),
  scenario("Female: 30 kg, verap", SEXF = 1, WT = 30, CONMED_VERAPAMIL = 1),
  scenario("Female: 12 y, 30 kg, verap", SEXF = 1, AGE = 12, WT = 30,
           CONMED_VERAPAMIL = 1),
  scenario("Female: 12 y, 30 kg, clari", SEXF = 1, AGE = 12, WT = 30,
           CONMED_CLARITHROMYCIN = 1)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

# The residual-error SDs are thetas, so only the omegas need zeroing.
mod_typical <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "omega"),
  warning = muffle_expected
)

ev_typ <- make_ss_events(scenarios, dose = 25)
sim_typ <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_typical, events = ev_typ, keep = "scenario",
    atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10
  ),
  warning = muffle_expected
) |>
  as.data.frame()

nca_typ <- ss_nca(sim_typ, ev_typ, "scenario")
typ <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax")) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

# The model's own closed form at steady state: AUCtau = F * dose / CL.
closed_form <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time == t_ss) |>
  dplyr::distinct(scenario, fdepot, cl) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_closed = 1000 * fdepot * 25 / cl)
typ <- dplyr::left_join(typ, closed_form, by = "scenario")

# Same parameters on both sides, so only trapezoid and solver error remain.
stopifnot(all(abs(typ$auclast / typ$auc_closed - 1) < 0.01))
```

```{r reference-check}
published_points <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                    ~auc_pub, ~cmax_pub,
  "Reference",                      3723,       246,
  "Female: 12 y, 30 kg, verap",    10630,      1003,
  "Female: 12 y, 30 kg, clari",    11700,       954
)
point_check <- typ |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_points, by = "scenario") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auclast / auc_pub - 1),
    cmax_pct = 100 * (cmax / cmax_pub - 1)
  )

point_check |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, auclast, auc_pub, auc_pct, cmax, cmax_pub, cmax_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario (25 mg once daily)" = scenario,
    "AUC24 model (ng h/mL)" = auclast,
    "AUC24 paper" = auc_pub,
    "AUC24 diff (%)" = auc_pct,
    "Cmax model (ng/mL)" = cmax,
    "Cmax paper" = cmax_pub,
    "Cmax diff (%)" = cmax_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value steady-state exposure against the values stated in the Usansky 2026 Results.")

# AUC is set by F, dose and CL alone, so a transcription error in any of them
# moves it by tens of percent. Cmax also carries the paper's simulated
# between-subject spread (its geometric mean is not exactly the typical value).
stopifnot(
  all(abs(point_check$auc_pct) < 5),
  all(abs(point_check$cmax_pct) < 15)
)
```

# Replicate Figures 3 and 4 (forest plots)

Figures 3 and 4 show, for each covariate scenario, the distribution of the
percent change in steady-state AUC24 and Cmax relative to the reference
subject. The medians below were digitised by the maintainers from the
published figures (read to about 5 percentage points). With log-normal random
effects the median change equals the typical-value change, which the model
gives directly.

```{r forest}

  "Fed",                                                                         0,         0,

  "Asian",                                                                     -20,       -12,
  "Hepatic impairment",                                                        -17,       -10,
  "Elderly: 85 years old",                                                       0,        -5,
  "Adolescent: 12 years old",                                                    0,        22,
  "Elderly female: 85 years old",                                               10,         0,
  "Adolescent female: 12 years old",                                            10,        30,
  "Black male: 155 kg, rif, hepatically impaired",                             -77,       -70,

ref <- dplyr::filter(typ, scenario == "Reference")
forest <- typ |>
  dplyr::filter(scenario != "Reference") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc_model = 100 * (auclast / ref$auclast - 1),
    cmax_model = 100 * (cmax / ref$cmax - 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(digitised, by = "scenario") |>
  dplyr::mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = rev(digitised$scenario)))
stopifnot(nrow(forest) == nrow(digitised))

forest |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, auc_fig, auc_model, cmax_fig, cmax_model) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-scenario, names_to = c("metric", "source"),
                      names_sep = "_") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = ifelse(metric == "auc", "AUC24 (Figure 3)", "Cmax (Figure 4)"),
    source = ifelse(source == "fig", "Published median (digitised)",
                    "Packaged model, typical value")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(value, scenario, shape = source, colour = source)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Change relative to the reference subject (%)", y = NULL,
       shape = NULL, colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the medians of Figures 3 and 4 of Usansky 2026.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r forest-check}
forest_check <- forest |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_diff = auc_model - auc_fig, cmax_diff = cmax_model - cmax_fig)

forest_check |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(scenario)) |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, auc_fig, auc_model, cmax_fig, cmax_model) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "AUC24 change, Figure 3 (%)" = auc_fig,
    "AUC24 change, model (%)" = auc_model,
    "Cmax change, Figure 4 (%)" = cmax_fig,
    "Cmax change, model (%)" = cmax_model
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 0, caption = "Percent change in steady-state exposure from the reference subject.")

# The two 85-year-old 'nonfasting' rows are a known deviation (see
# Assumptions and deviations): steady-state AUC does not depend on age or food
# in the published equations, yet the figure places these rows about 15 points
# above the matching rows without age and food.
aligned <- forest_check |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("nonfasting", scenario))
stopifnot(
  abs(median(aligned$auc_diff)) < 5,
  max(abs(aligned$auc_diff)) < 15,
  abs(median(aligned$cmax_diff)) < 10
)
```

# Replicate Table 3 (ASPEN steady-state exposure)

Table 3 gives the steady-state exposure of the ASPEN participants, derived from
their individual model parameters. The virtual ASPEN cohort below takes its
covariates from the adult and adolescent columns of Table 1: log-normal body
weight (adults 69.8 kg, CV 22.2%; adolescents 50.4 kg, CV 24.8%), age (adults
normal with mean 52.9 and SD 19.5 years truncated to 18-85; adolescents uniform
12-17 years), the tabulated sex and race fractions, the phase 3 tablet taken
fasted, no interacting comedication, and the phase 3 residual-error stratum.

```{r aspen-cohort}
set.seed(20261117)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261117)

make_aspen <- function(n, adolescent, dose, id_offset) {
  if (adolescent) {
    wt <- exp(rnorm(n, log(50.4) - 0.5 * log(1 + 0.248^2), sqrt(log(1 + 0.248^2))))
    age <- runif(n, 12, 17.99)
    p_female <- 0.419
    p_black <- 0
    p_asian <- 0.0323
  } else {
    wt <- exp(rnorm(n, log(69.8) - 0.5 * log(1 + 0.222^2), sqrt(log(1 + 0.222^2))))
    age <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 52.9, 19.5), 18), 85)
    p_female <- 0.558
    p_black <- 0.062
    p_asian <- 0.118
  }
  race <- sample(c("black", "asian", "other"), n, replace = TRUE,
                 prob = c(p_black, p_asian, 1 - p_black - p_asian))
  subjects <- tibble::tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    group = paste(if (adolescent) "Adolescents" else "Adults", paste0(dose, " mg")),
    WT = wt, AGE = age, SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, p_female),
    RACE_BLACK = as.integer(race == "black"),
    RACE_ASIAN = as.integer(race == "asian"),
    HEPIMP = 0, FED = 0, FORM_SOLUTION = 0, CONMED_RIFAMPICIN = 0,
    CONMED_CLARITHROMYCIN = 0, CONMED_VERAPAMIL = 0,
    STUDY_PHASE2 = 0, STUDY_PHASE3 = 1, OCC = 1
  )
  make_ss_events(subjects, dose = dose, obs_step = 0.25)
}

ev_aspen <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_aspen(200, FALSE, 10, 0L),
  make_aspen(200, FALSE, 25, 200L),
  make_aspen(100, TRUE, 10, 400L),
  make_aspen(100, TRUE, 25, 500L)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_aspen[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_aspen <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_aspen, keep = "group"),
  warning = muffle_expected
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r aspen-profiles}
sim_aspen |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_ss) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(x = "Time after the dose at steady state (h)",
       y = "Brensocatib plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Median and 90% interval of the model-predicted steady-state profile (no residual error).")
```

```{r aspen-nca}
nca_aspen <- ss_nca(sim_aspen, ev_aspen, "group")

geo_mean <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))
sim_gm <- as.data.frame(nca_aspen) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "tmax", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(value = geo_mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = value)

table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,               ~auclast, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~cmin,
  "Adults 10 mg",           1360,  85.4,  1.19,  40.0,
  "Adults 25 mg",           4060,   259,  1.20,   119,
  "Adolescents 10 mg",      1620,   123, 0.994,  42.9,
  "Adolescents 25 mg",      5650,   419,  1.39,   148
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_gm,
  reference = table3,
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h", cmin = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. Usansky 2026 Table 3 steady-state geometric means. * differs by >20%.")
```

The individual parameters behind Table 3 can be compared the same way.

```{r aspen-params}
param_gm <- sim_aspen |>
  dplyr::filter(time == t_ss) |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cl_model = geo_mean(cl),
    vss_model = geo_mean(vc + vp),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~group,              ~cl_pub, ~vss_pub,
      "Adults 10 mg",         2.81,      126,
      "Adults 25 mg",         3.02,      131,
      "Adolescents 10 mg",    2.36,     83.6,
      "Adolescents 25 mg",    2.07,     71.3
    ),
    by = "group"
  )

param_gm |>
  dplyr::select(group, cl_model, cl_pub, vss_model, vss_pub) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group,
    "CL/F model (L/h)" = cl_model,
    "CL/F Table 3" = cl_pub,
    "Vss/F model (L)" = vss_model,
    "Vss/F Table 3" = vss_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Geometric-mean individual CL/F and Vss/F against Usansky 2026 Table 3.")

aspen_ratio <- sim_gm |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table3, by = "group", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    auc = auclast_sim / auclast_pub,
    cmax = cmax_sim / cmax_pub,
    adult = grepl("Adults", group)
  )
# Adults: 288-307 ASPEN patients per arm, so the published geometric means are
# precise and a structural error (CL, F, dose or units) would move AUC by tens
# of percent. Adolescents (15-16 per arm) are reported in the table above
# without a gate. The cohort-covariate mismatch puts AUC about 7-14% low
# (see below; realised AUC ratios 0.86 and 0.93, Cmax 0.90 and 0.97, the
# same at 2 and 16 threads), so the bound leaves room for the per-thread
# cohort draw while a mis-transcribed CL, F, dose or unit still breaks it.
adults <- dplyr::filter(aspen_ratio, adult)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(adults$auc - 1) < 0.25),
  all(abs(adults$cmax - 1) < 0.25)
)
```

The virtual cohort reproduces Cmax and Tmax closely and sits about 7-14% below
the published AUC24 and Cmin, with a geometric-mean CL/F 5-10% above the
published one. CL/F in the model depends on weight, sex and race, so the gap
reflects the difference between the pooled Table 1 covariates used here and the
actual ASPEN participants (for example a larger female fraction would lower
CL/F); the reference-subject check above, which needs no cohort assumptions,
agrees to within 2%. The adolescent 25 mg Tmax is starred against a published
value from 16 patients with a 57.6% geometric CV.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Variability values.** Usansky 2026 reports only the fixed effects of the
  final model (Table 2). The between-subject, between-occasion and residual
  variances are taken from the `$OMEGA` and `$SIGMA` records of the final
  control stream published as Data S1. In that file the non-fixed `$THETA`
  records are starting values from a closely preceding run (for example CL/F
  3.18 against the final 3.25 L/h, Vc/F 81.7 against 78.8 L, and the age
  exponent 0.371 against 0.314), so the variances are very probably also
  starting values that differ by a few percent from the final estimates. They
  are the authors' own values and the closest available; the maintainers chose
  them over removing the variability. IIV on Q/F is fixed to zero in the
  control stream and is omitted.
- **Hepatic impairment.** The printed CL/F equation writes the hepatic factor
  as 1.187^HI with HI the "Child-Pugh classification number", which would
  compound the effect by grade. The control stream applies one factor of
  (1 + 0.187) to any impairment (`IF(CPCLASSN.NE.0)`), the estimate came from a
  single study with 6 participants per grade, and Table 2 lists one
  coefficient; the control stream form is used, through the binary `HEPIMP`.
- **Comedications.** The source codes rifampicin, clarithromycin and verapamil
  as levels of one categorical column, so at most one of the three
  `CONMED_*` indicators should be 1 at a time. Their effects were fixed from
  dedicated interaction studies, as were the hepatic-impairment effect.
- **Occasions.** The control stream carries between-occasion variability on ka
  and relative bioavailability for occasions 1 and 2 with a shared variance;
  the paper does not define an occasion. Records with any other `OCC` carry no
  between-occasion deviation. The simulations here put every record in
  occasion 1. Because the occasion terms enter as an indicator-weighted sum,
  rxode2 reports those etas as non-mu-referenced; this affects only
  estimation speed-ups, not simulation.
- **Forest-plot rows with age 85 and fed dosing.** In the published equations
  steady-state AUC24 depends only on dose, bioavailability and CL/F, so adding
  age 85 and a fed dose to the 155 kg / rifampicin / hepatic-impairment rows
  cannot change it. Figure 3 nevertheless places those two rows about 15
  percentage points above the matching rows without age and food, while every
  other row agrees with the model to within the digitising error. The reason is
  not stated; the two rows are shown but excluded from the forest-plot check.
- **Figure medians.** Figure 3 and 4 medians were digitised by the maintainers
  from the published images, to about 5 percentage points.
- **ASPEN virtual cohort.** Table 1 gives covariates for adults pooled across
  all 11 trials rather than for ASPEN alone; those are used. Age is assumed
  normal (truncated 18-85) in adults and uniform in adolescents, and every
  dose is taken fasted as the phase 3 tablet. Table 3 is derived from the
  individual parameter estimates of the observed patients, so it reflects the
  ASPEN covariate mix exactly, which the virtual cohort only approximates.
- **No erratum** was found for Usansky 2026 as of 2026-11-17.
